sources.README.md:
# Editorial rights review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

React JSX imperative handle uses a ref for synchronous visit entry; component cleanup retires view while service queue retains receipt values.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

checkpoints: Several edits within 120 ms produce no early write and one write containing the latest text after the quiet interval.
A later editing burst independently saves after its own 120 ms quiet interval.
Closing or switching documents preserves pending edited text; reopening restores that text.
Submitting with pending edits preserves the submission-entry snapshot and returns its receipt, including when save or archive subscribers synchronously navigate.
A confirmation from a retired visit does not appear in a later visit, including reopening the same document.
Search preview retains its 40 ms delay, cancellation on hide, and usability for later queries.
forbidden_effects: Writing the document store on every keystroke.
Losing pending document edits when their editor visit ends.
Allowing pending work from an earlier visit to overwrite newer persisted edits.
Publishing a submission confirmation into a different editor visit.
Changing the adjacent search preview or synchronous public interfaces.
Treating AST hints, experience, automatic contracts, or evaluation observations as normative requirements.
lifecycle_identity: Each editor opening is a fresh visit, even when its document identifier matches an earlier opening.
Pending document saves belong to the visit and document that received the edits.
A submission snapshot belongs to the visit active at submission entry; durable receipt retention and confirmation visibility have separate lifetimes.
Confirmation ownership is acquired when bindConfirmation is called and uses visit object identity.

Keep existing injected interfaces, integration cleanup, fresh-visit semantics, receipt retention, and search-preview behavior.
